# hackerscad for agents

hackerscad builds CAD models from .hcad files, a sandboxed subset of D.
Typical loop: read this reference, write a model, call hcad_render to get
dimensions and pictures, compare them with the request, fix, then export.

## Rules that avoid most mistakes
- Every exported body is a function marked @part that takes no arguments and
  returns a Solid, with the annotation on its own line:
      @part("steelblue")
      Solid body() { ... }
- Reference objects (the shaft a knob fits on, the phone a stand holds) are
  parts too, see-through and not exported, so the fit can be checked:
      @part("slategray", alpha: 0.4, export: false)
- Lengths: write units (60.mm, 2.5.cm, 1.inch). Bare numbers passed to
  geometry are millimetres. Never add a bare number to a length (60.mm + 5 is
  an error; write 60.mm + 5.mm).
- Angles: rotate(z: 45) uses degrees; 30.deg is explicit.
- Primitives stand on the XY plane and are centred in X and Y:
  box(x, y, z) spans z = 0 .. z; cylinder(r: or d:, h:) also; center: true
  centres in Z. sphere(r) is centred on the origin.
- Booleans: a + b (union), a - b (difference), a & b (intersection).
- Place parts relative to each other instead of computing coordinates:
  lid.nextTo(body, X, gap: 10.mm), cap.on(body).
- Fillets, chamfers and shells take selectors, evaluated on the solid they
  apply to: .fillet(edges.parallel(Z), r: 3.mm),
  .chamfer(edges.filter(e => e.mid.z > 5.mm), d: 1.mm),
  .shell(open: faces.top, thickness: 2.mm). Apply fillets before shell and
  before cutting holes; a fillet radius must be smaller than the faces next
  to the edge.
- To round or chamfer the edges a cut left behind, select them by provenance:
  .fillet(edges.between(faces.from(holes), faces.top), r: 0.5.mm).
- Cut with planes: body.split(body.plane(faces.top).offset(-10.mm)) gives
  .above and .below; s.pieces lists separate bodies, ordered along X, Y, Z.
- Profiles: rect, circle, polygon, regularPolygon, slot, text, combined
  with + - &, .round(r), .offset(d); turn them into solids with .extrude(h)
  or .revolve(axis: Y). On a face: body.extrude(profile, on: frame, depth:)
  adds, body.cut(profile, on: frame, depth: | through: true) removes.
- Sweeps and lofts: circle(d: 4.mm).sweep(path([vec(0, 0, 0), vec(0, 0, 30),
  vec(30, 0, 30)])), circle(d: 1.mm).sweep(helix(r: 5.mm, pitch: 2.mm,
  height: 20.mm), frenet: true), loft([circle(r: 20), rect(25).move(z: 40)]).
- Exact 2D outlines with dimensions: auto s = sketch(); points, lines, arcs,
  circles, then constraints (horizontal, vertical, length, distance, angle,
  tangent, equal…) and s.profile. Prefer it when a request gives dimensions
  of an irregular outline; a warning lists points left free.
- To build on a face, take its frame and place parts built on XY (Z up):
  cylinder(d: 8.mm, h: 5.mm).placeOn(body.frame(faces.top).at(x: 10.mm)).
- Axes and planes anywhere: rotate(90.deg, axis: body.axis(edges.filter(e =>
  e.isCircle && e.radius == 3.mm))), s.mirror(plane(origin: vec(10, 0, 0),
  normal: X)), plane(p1, p2, p3), plane(axis, point).
- Existing parts: load("part.stl"/".obj"/".3mf"/".step", scale: 1) gives a solid to
  modify; text("LABEL", size: 4.mm).centered centres a profile for engraving.
- Constants are immutable; module-level values cannot be modified.
- Expose the dimensions a user may want to change as parameters:
      @param("Outer width", min: 20.mm, max: 200.mm)
      immutable width = 60.mm;
  and put requirements in unittest blocks:
  unittest { assert(body.bbox.size.z <= 40.mm, "must fit in the drawer"); }
- Use the libraries instead of modelling common parts by hand:
  import hardware : M3, screw, nut, hole; then M3.clearance, M3.tap,
  screw(M3, 20.mm), nut(M3), hole(M3, 5.mm, "counterbore"|"insert"|…);
  import threads (threadedRod, tappedHole); import gears (spurGear, rack,
  centerDistance); import hinges (hinge(…).fixed/.moving, print in place);
  import snaps (snapHook, snapSlot); import enclosures (roundedBox, tray,
  enclosure(vec(x, y, z)).base/.lid).
- Functions are ordinary arguments: xs.map(x => x * 2), xs.filter(f).
- Your own modules: import parts.bracket; is parts/bracket.hcad next to the
  model; import pizza; is pizza.hcad or pizza/package.hcad (which can
  public import its modules), also from the personal library folder.
- Strings interpolate: writeln("volume: $(body.volume)"); text("…", size:)
  is a 2D text profile, not a string function.
- Errors come with a line, a column and often a suggestion: apply it.
- Technical drawings: a function marked @drawing returns drawing(title: …),
  filled with d.standardViews(part) (views, overall dimensions, hole
  callouts) and d.section(part, XZ, label: "A"); export it as .pdf/.svg/.dxf.
- Keep models quick to evaluate: text cut into curved faces and threads take
  seconds; prefer text in relief as a separate part, and plain holes or
  heat-set inserts (hole(M3, d, "insert")) to modelled threads.
- Style: annotations (@param, @preset, @part, @drawing) go on their own line above
  the declaration, several per line when short; chains break before each
  call, the line starting with the dot.

# The `.hcad` language

A `.hcad` file is an **interpreted, sandboxed subset of D**. Anyone who knows D can read it without
surprises. There is no compilation step: the interpreter runs inside hackerscad and re-evaluates a
model in milliseconds.

## What stays the same as D
- **Lexical:** identifiers; numbers (`42`, `1_000`, `2.5`, `0xFF`, `2.5e3`); strings `"…"`, `` `…` ``, `r"…"` (the last two WYSIWYG as in D); comments `//`, `/* */` and nested `/+ +/`.
- **Declarations:** `immutable`, `const`, `auto`, typed variables, `struct` (fields, defaults, methods), functions (with `{ … }` or `=> expr;` bodies), `import`, `unittest`, UDAs.
- **Statements:** `if`/`else`, `foreach` (`foreach (i, x; arr)`, `foreach (i; 0 .. n)`, `foreach_reverse`), `for`, `while`, `break`, `continue`, `return`, `assert`, `switch` (with `case a, b:` and `default:`).
- **Assignments:** `=`, `+=`, `-=`, `*=`, `/=`, `%=`, `~=`, `++`, `--`.
- **Expressions:**
  - D precedence, including `^^`; ternary `?:`.
  - UFCS: `x.f(y)` is `f(x, y)`.
  - Named arguments: `f(x: 1)`.
  - Lambdas: `x => e`, `(a, b) => e`, `(int x) { return x; }`.
  - Functions are ordinary arguments: `xs.map(x => x * 2)`, `xs.map(&twice)`.
  - Array literals `[1, 2]` and associative literals `["a": 1]`.
  - Slices `a[1 .. $]`, concatenation `~`, `in`.
  - Struct literals `Screw("M3", 3.mm)` or `Screw(d: 3.mm)`.
- **Paren-less calls:** a declared function whose parameters all have defaults is called when named without parentheses (`body.bbox`, `nextTo(body, …)`). Use `&f` to pass the function itself.
- **Modules:**
  - `import std.math;`, `import hardware : M3;`, `import hw = hardware;`, `import lib.hinges;`, `import a, b;`.
  - `lib.hinges` resolves to `lib/hinges.hcad`; a folder is a package: `import pizza;` loads `pizza.hcad`, or else `pizza/package.hcad`, whose `public import pizza.base, pizza.toppings;` makes their names visible to whoever imports `pizza` (as in D).
  - Modules are looked for in the directory of the model, then in the folders of `$HCAD_PATH`, then in the personal library folder: `~/.local/share/hackerscad/lib` on Linux (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/hackerscad/lib`), `~/Library/Application Support/hackerscad/lib` on macOS, `%APPDATA%\hackerscad\lib` on Windows. The built-in libraries (`hardware`, `gears`…) come first.
  - `private` symbols are not exported.

## What is different from D
- **Strings interpolate:** `"volume: $(body.volume)"` inserts the value of the expression; `\$` is a literal dollar. Backtick and `r"…"` strings are WYSIWYG and never interpolate.
- **`~` joins anything with a string:** `"side " ~ width` gives `"side 60 mm"` (in D both sides must be strings).
- **Dynamic typing with run-time checks.**
  - `auto` works everywhere.
  - Declared types (`Length h`, `Solid f()`) are checked on calls, returns and assignments, with clear errors.
  - There are no templates: functions are passed as normal arguments (`xs.filter(x => x > 0)`). `!` is only used for type conversions (`to!string`).
- **Value semantics.** Arrays, associative arrays and structs behave as values: `b = a; b[0] = 9;` does not change `a`.
- **Purity.**
  - Locals inside functions are mutable.
  - Module-level declarations (`immutable`, and even `auto`) are read-only and evaluated lazily, in any order. Constants use `immutable`; `enum` is reserved for enumerations.
  - Every function is therefore deterministic, and results can be cached. This is the basis of incremental regeneration.
- **Not available:** classes, pointers, `mixin`, `static if`, user templates, exceptions, `asm`, `alias`, `new`.
- **Sandbox.**
  - `load()` reads mesh and STEP files inside the project directory only.
  - Library imports are limited to hackerscad's standard modules: `std.shapes`, `std.math`, `std.algorithm`, `std.range`, `std.conv`, `std.format`, `std.stdio`, `std.array`, and `hardware`.
  - Imports cannot leave the project directory or the library folder they were found in.
  - There is no file, network or process access.
  - Evaluation steps, recursion depth and array sizes are limited.
- **`writeln`** writes to hackerscad's console (and to the JSON output for agents), not to stdout.

## hackerscad additions
- **Units** are UFCS functions: `60.mm`, `2.5.cm`, `1.m`, `1.inch`, `45.deg`, `0.5.rad`.
  - Values carry a dimension (`Length`, `Angle`, `Area`, `Volume`), and arithmetic checks it: `Length * Length` is an `Area`, while `60.mm + 45.deg` is an error.
  - **Bare numbers** passed where a length is expected use the file's default unit: `mm`, or the unit set with `@unit(inch) module name;`. Values keep their unit, so libraries written with different default units combine correctly.
  - Mixing bare and dimensioned numbers in arithmetic (`60.mm + 5`) is an error. Scaling is fine (`2 * 60.mm`).
  - Bare angles passed to features (`rotate(z: 45)`) are degrees. `sin`/`cos` take radians for bare numbers, as in D.
- **Vectors:** `vec(10.mm, 5.mm)`, `vec(x, y, z)`, with `.x .y .z .xy .length .normalized`, `dot`, `cross`, `distance`. Vectors compare with a small tolerance.
- **Directions:** `X`, `Y`, `Z`, `-X`…
- **`@param("description", min:, max:, step:, choices:)`** above **`immutable name = default;`** declares a parameter. It can be overridden from the GUI, from the CLI (`-D name=80.mm`, or `-D name=80` in the model unit) and by agents, and is checked against its limits.
- **`@preset("name", value)`** on a parameter gives its value in a named preset (`--preset name`, or the preset menu in the GUI). A preset is the set of values declared under its name; parameters without a value for it keep their default.
  - Parameters never change during an evaluation: their value is decided beforehand, from default, then preset, then explicit override.
  - Like a configuration table: every parameter is a column, every preset a row.
- **`@part("colour")`** above **`Solid name() { … }`** declares an exported body: a separate object in 3MF, and part of the STEP. A part is evaluated once per run even when other parts refer to it. Without a colour a part is mint (`#8FCBB4`). `@part("slategray", alpha: 0.4)` makes it see-through; `export: false` makes it a reference part (a shaft, a board, the object a holder is for): drawn in the view and in PNGs, left out of STL, 3MF and STEP.
- **Colours** are CSS names (`"steelblue"`), `"#RRGGBB"`, `"#RRGGBBAA"` (the last byte is the opacity) or `rgb(r, g, b)` with 0…255 channels, `rgb(r, g, b, alpha: 0.5)`. `solid.color("orange", alpha: 0.5)` works too.
- **`unittest { assert(…); }`** blocks are design checks. They run after evaluation; a failure does not discard the geometry, but is reported in the GUI, the CLI and to agents.
- **Solids and booleans:**
  - `a + b` union, `a - b` difference, `a & b` intersection; `s += x` inside functions.
  - `Solid.init` and `nothing` are the empty solid. `solids.sum` and `fuse(…)` unite arrays.
- **Primitives** stand on the XY plane, centred in X and Y; `center: true` centres them in Z too. Spheres are centred.
  - `box(x, y, z)`, `cylinder(r | d, h)`, `cone(r1 | d1, r2 | d2, h)`, `sphere(r | d)`.
- **Profiles** (2D shapes on the XY plane, type `Profile`):
  - `rect(w, h)` and `circle(r | d)` centred on the origin; `polygon([vec(0, 0), vec(30, 0), vec(0, 20)])`; `regularPolygon(6, d: 10.mm)` (d/r through the corners); `slot(length, width)` (a stadium along X); `text("text", size: 10.mm, font: "Sans")` (starting at the origin on the baseline).
  - Combine with `+ - &`, move/rotate/mirror like solids; `.round(r)` rounds the corners; `.offset(d)` grows (d > 0) or shrinks it; `.area`.
  - `.extrude(h)` makes a solid along +Z (negative h goes down); options `taper: 3.deg` (sides narrow towards the top), `symmetric: true`. Extrude while the profile lies on XY, then place the solid.
  - `.revolve()`: turned around the axis, standing up: the profile's x is the radius and its y the height along Z (pots, bottles, knobs). `.revolve(axis: X, angle: 180.deg)`: around an axis in the profile's plane (a direction through the origin or an `Axis`), without standing up; `angle:` turns less than all the way.
  - On a face or plane, add or remove material in one step: `body.extrude(profile, on: frame, depth: 5.mm)` grows outwards along the frame's Z; `body.cut(profile, on: frame, depth: 2.mm)` digs in, `through: true` cuts all the way. Both accept `taper:`.
- **Paths, sweeps and lofts:**
  - Paths (type `Path`): `path([vec(0, 0, 0), vec(0, 0, 20), vec(30, 0, 20)])` (straight segments, mitred corners; `closed: true`), `spline([…])` (a smooth curve through the points), `helix(r | d, pitch:, height:, left: false)` (around +Z, starting at (r, 0, 0)). Paths move, rotate and mirror like solids.
  - `profile.sweep(path)`: the profile, drawn on XY around the origin, starts at the beginning of the path, normal to it, with its +Y kept towards world +Z (towards +Y when the path starts vertically). `frenet: true` follows the curvature (use it for helices: springs, threads). Holes in the profile give tubes.
  - `loft([circle(r: 20), rect(30).move(z: 40), circle(r: 10).move(z: 80)])`: a smooth solid through profiles placed in space; `ruled: true` gives flat sides. Profiles with holes are lofted as tubes when every profile has the same number of holes.
- **Constrained sketches** (2D on XY): `auto s = sketch();` then add geometry and constraints and take `s.profile`.
  - Geometry: `s.point(x, y)` (where it starts: constraints move it; `fixed: true` pins it there), `s.line(p, q)`, `s.arc(center, start, end)` (counter-clockwise), `s.circle(center, r: | d:)` (without r/d the radius is left to the constraints), `s.polyline([p1, p2, vec(…)], closed: true)` (returns the lines; vectors become new points). `construction: true` geometry helps constraining but is not part of the outline.
  - Constraints: `coincident(p, q)`, `fix(p)`, `horizontal(line | p, q)`, `vertical(…)`, `length(line, v)`, `distance(p, q, v)`, `distance(p, q, v, along: X | Y)`, `distance(p, line, v)`, `on(p, line | circle | arc)`, `parallel(a, b)`, `perpendicular(a, b)`, `angle(a, b, v)` (between the line directions, start → end), `equal(a, b)` (lengths or radii), `radius(c, v)`, `diameter(c, v)`, `tangent(line | circle, circle | line)`, `midpoint(p, line)`, `symmetric(p, q, line)`.
  - `s.fillet(p, r)` rounds the corner where two lines meet at p.
  - Reading back: `p.x`, `p.y`, `p.pos`, `line.start`, `line.end`, `line.length`, `line.mid`, `c.center`, `c.radius`, `s.dof` (degrees of freedom left), `s.solved`.
  - `s.profile` solves and returns the closed loops of non-construction lines, arcs and circles as a `Profile` (inner loops are holes). Under-constrained sketches still work, with a warning listing the lines of the free points; conflicting constraints are an error pointing at them.
- **Transforms:** `move(v | x:, y:, z:)`, `rotate(x:, y:, z:)` or `rotate(angle, axis:)` (a direction through the origin, or an `Axis` anywhere), `scale(k)`, `mirror(X)` (plane through the origin with that normal) or `mirror(plane)` (any plane), `color(c)`.
- **Placement:** `a.nextTo(b, X, gap: 10.mm)`, `a.on(b)`, `a.align(b, x: "center", z: "min")` (each axis `"min"`, `"center"` or `"max"` of the bounding boxes).
- **Patterns:** `hole.linearPattern(4, step: vec(10, 0, 0))`, `peg.circularPattern(6, axis: Z, angle: 360.deg)` give one solid with all the copies (subtract it to cut them all).
- **Axes:** `axis(origin: vec(10, 0, 0), direction: Z)`, `axis(p1, p2)` (through two points), `body.axis(edges.filter(…))` (the line of a straight edge, or the centre and normal of a circular one such as a hole rim), `frame.axis(X)` (an axis of a frame). Fields: `origin`, `direction`. Use them with `rotate(angle, axis: a)` and `circularPattern(n, axis: a)`.
- **Planes:** `XY`, `XZ`, `YZ`, `plane(origin: vec(0, 0, 10), normal: Z)`, `plane(p1, p2, p3)` (three points; the normal follows p1 → p2 → p3 by the right-hand rule), `plane(axis, point)` (containing a line and a point), or the plane of a face: `body.plane(faces.top)`. Planes also mirror: `s.mirror(plane)`.
  - `p.offset(5.mm)` is the parallel plane moved along the normal (negative goes the other way); `p.flip` reverses the normal.
  - Fields: `origin`, `normal`.
- **Frames** (an origin and X, Y, Z axes) to build on faces and planes:
  - `body.frame(faces.top)`: origin at the face centre, Z along the outward normal, X along the global X projected on the face (global Y if X is perpendicular). Options: `origin: vec(…)` (projected on the face), `x: Y`.
  - `plane.frame(origin: vec(…), x: …)`: on a plane the origin defaults to the plane's origin; give a point to choose another one.
  - `World` is the global frame; `f.at(x: 10, y: -5)` moves the origin in local coordinates; `f.turn(30.deg)` rotates X and Y around Z. Fields: `origin`, `x`, `y`, `z`.
  - `solid.placeOn(f)`: a solid built on XY with Z up is moved onto the frame. A plane works too (`placeOn(plane)`): its origin is the zero and X is the global X projected on it. A boss: `cylinder(d: 8, h: 5).placeOn(f)`; a pocket: `body - box(10, 10, 3).move(z: -3).placeOn(f)`.
- **Cutting:** `s.split(plane)` returns both sides: `.above` (where the normal points) and `.below`.
- **Separate bodies:** `s.pieces` lists the disconnected bodies of a solid (e.g. after a cut through it), ordered by position along X, then Y, then Z; pick one with `[i]` or sort them (`s.pieces.sort((a, b) => a.volume > b.volume)`).
- **Importing parts:** `load("part.stl")`, `load("part.obj")`, `load("part.3mf")`, `load("part.step")`, with `scale:` (STL and OBJ are read in mm; 3MF uses its own unit and build transforms). Meshes become solids (coplanar triangles merged into faces, closed meshes only), STEP files keep their exact geometry; both can be cut, filleted, measured and selected like any other solid. Paths are relative to the model file and must stay inside the project directory.
- **Centring:** `shape.centered` moves a profile (in X and Y) or a solid (in X, Y and Z) so its bounding box is centred on the origin, e.g. `text("LABEL", size: 4.mm).centered`.
- **Measuring:** `distance(a, b)` between two solids (0 when they touch), `s.bbox`, `s.volume`, `s.area`.
- **Introspection:** `s.bbox` (`min`, `max`, `size`, `center`), `s.volume`, `s.area`, `s.isValid`.
- **Features:** `fillet(edges, r:)`, `chamfer(edges, d:)`, `shell(open: faces, thickness:)`, `draft(faces, angle:, pull: Z, neutral: 0.mm)` (mould taper around the neutral plane).
- **Face provenance:** every face remembers the feature that created it (primitive, fillet, shell, split…). Clicking a face in the GUI highlights it and jumps to that line.
- **Topological selectors** are resolved against the solid the feature is applied to:
  - predicates: `edges.filter(e => e.isParallel(Z))`, `faces.filter(f => f.normal == Z)`;
  - shortcuts: `edges.parallel(Z)`, `edges.perpendicular(Z)`, `edges.lines`, `edges.circles`, `faces.top/bottom/left/right/front/back`, `faces.normal(X)`, `faces.largest`;
  - by provenance: `faces.from(tool)` (faces created by a tool or feature, e.g. the walls of the holes cut with it), `edges.from(tool)` (edges between two such faces);
  - by adjacency: `edges.of(faces.top)` (edges touching those faces), `edges.between(faces.from(holes), faces.top)` (the rim of the holes on the top face);
  - edge properties: `start`, `end`, `mid`, `direction`, `length`, `isLine`, `isCircle`, `isParallel(axis)`, `isPerpendicular(axis)`, and for circles `center`, `axis`, `radius` (e.g. `edges.filter(e => e.isCircle && e.radius == 3.mm)`);
  - face properties: `center`, `normal`, `area`.
- **Built-in libraries** (`import gears;` or `import std.gears;`, selective imports work too):
  - `hardware`: `Screw` sizes `M2`, `M2_5`, `M3`, `M4`, `M5`, `M6`, `M8` with `d`, `pitch`, `tap`, `clearance`, `head`, `headHeight`, `key`, `nut`, `nutHeight`, `washer`, `insert`, `insertDepth`; `screw(M3, 20.mm, threaded: false)` (socket head cap screw, underside of the head on z = 0), `nut(M3, threaded: false)`, `washer(M3)`, `hexPrism(acrossFlats, h)`; tools to subtract, top on z = 0 going down: `hole(M3, depth, "clearance" | "tap" | "insert" | "counterbore" | "countersink")`, `nutTrap(M3, depth)`.
  - `threads`: `threadedRod(d, pitch, length, chamfer: true, left: false)` (ISO metric profile, real geometry), `tappedHole(d, pitch, depth, clearance: 0.15.mm)` (a tool to subtract for an internal thread), `toothHeight(pitch)`. Threads take a second or two to compute.
  - `gears`: `spurGear(m, teeth, thickness, bore: 0.mm, pressure: 20.deg, backlash: 0.1.mm)` (involute, centred, a tooth on +X), `gearProfile(m, teeth, …)`, `rack(m, teeth, thickness)`, `pitchDiameter`, `outsideDiameter`, `rootDiameter`, `centerDistance(m, z1, z2)` (where to put two meshing gears; turn the second by half a tooth: `rotate(z: 180.deg / z2)`).
  - `hinges`: `hinge(length:, width:, thickness:, knuckles: 5, clearance: 0.4.mm)` returns `.fixed` and `.moving`, two leaves printed in place around an axis along X at z = thickness.
  - `snaps`: `snapHook(length:, thickness:, width:, overhang:, lead: 30.deg)` (a cantilever hook standing on z = 0, barb towards +X) and `snapSlot(…)` (the window to subtract from the mating wall).
  - `enclosures`: `roundedBox(x, y, z, r)`, `tray(x, y, z, wall:, r:)` (open on top), `enclosure(vec(x, y, z), wall:, r:, lidHeight:, screw: M3)` returns `.base` and `.lid` (lid with a lip that fits inside, screw posts in the corners).
- **Drawings** (technical sheets, exported as SVG, PDF or DXF): a function marked `@drawing` returns `drawing(size: "A4", title:, author:, material:, projection: "first" | "third", scale: 0 (fit), landscape: true)` after adding to it:
  - `d.standardViews(solid, iso: true, dimensions: true)`: front, top, side and an isometric view, laid out and scaled to fit, with overall dimensions and hole callouts;
  - `d.view(solid, "front" | "back" | "top" | "bottom" | "right" | "left" | "iso", at: vec(x, y), scale:)` (without `at:` the layout places it; `at:` is in paper mm from the bottom-left corner);
  - `d.section(solid, plane, label: "A")`: the solid cut by the plane, seen from the side the normal points to, cut faces hatched;
  - `d.dimension(view, from: vec(…), to: vec(…), offset: 8.mm, text:)` between two model points, on a view returned by `view`/`standardViews`; `d.note("text", at: vec(x, y), size: 3.5.mm)`.
  - `hscad render model.hcad -o sheet.pdf` exports the first drawing, `--drawing name` another one.
- **Standard algorithms** (eager, Phobos names, functions as normal arguments): `map`, `filter`, `fold`, `sum`, `any`, `all`, `count`, `canFind`, `sort`, `reverse`, `iota`, `cartesianProduct`, `zip`, `enumerate`, `join`, `min`, `max`, `minElement`, `maxElement`, `clamp`, `to!T`, `format`.

## Style

- Annotations (`@param`, `@preset`, `@part`, `@drawing`) go on their own line, above what they annotate; short ones share a line (`@preset("small", 40.mm) @preset("large", 120.mm)`), long ones get one line each.
- Long chains break before each call, the new line starting with the dot:

```d
@part("steelblue")
Solid block() => box(40, 30, 20)
    .fillet(edges.parallel(Z), r: 3.mm)
    .shell(open: faces.top, thickness: 2.mm);
```

## Example
See [examples/box.hcad](../examples/box.hcad).

## Example: box with lid

```d
// Parametric box with lid: the first example in the D-like style.
module box;

import std.shapes;
import hardware : M3, Screw;

// Each parameter lists its own presets: @preset("name", value).
@param("Outer width", min: 20.mm, max: 200.mm)
@preset("small", 40.mm) @preset("large", 120.mm)
immutable width = 60.mm;

@param("Outer depth", min: 20.mm, max: 200.mm)
@preset("small", 30.mm)
immutable depth = 40.mm;

@param("Height", min: 10.mm, max: 100.mm)
@preset("large", 40.mm)
immutable height = 25.mm;

@param("Wall thickness", min: 1.2.mm, max: 4.mm)
immutable wall = 2.mm;

@param("Corner radius", min: 3.mm, max: 15.mm)
@preset("small", 4.mm)
immutable radius = 6.mm;

/// Post for a self-tapping screw, with a pilot hole.
Solid post(Length h, Screw screw = M3)
{
    return cylinder(d: screw.d * 2.2, h: h) - cylinder(d: screw.tap, h: h + 1.mm);
}

@part("steelblue")
Solid body()
{
    auto s = box(width, depth, height)
        .fillet(edges.filter(e => e.isParallel(Z)), r: radius)
        .shell(open: faces.top, thickness: wall);

    // one post in each corner, centred on the corner fillet
    immutable dx = width / 2 - radius, dy = depth / 2 - radius;
    foreach (sx; [-1, 1])
        foreach (sy; [-1, 1])
            s += post(height - 3.mm).move(x: sx * dx, y: sy * dy);

    return s;
}

@part("orange")
Solid lid()
{
    auto c = box(width, depth, wall)
        .fillet(edges.parallel(Z), r: radius)
        .chamfer(edges.filter(e => e.mid.z > wall / 2), d: 0.6.mm);   // the whole top edge

    immutable dx = width / 2 - radius, dy = depth / 2 - radius;
    foreach (sx; [-1, 1])
        foreach (sy; [-1, 1])
            c -= cylinder(d: M3.clearance, h: 3 * wall, center: true).move(x: sx * dx, y: sy * dy);

    return c.nextTo(body, X, gap: 10.mm);
}

unittest
{
    assert(body.bbox.size.z <= 40.mm, "must fit in the drawer");
    writeln("body volume: $(format("%.1f", body.volume / 1.cm ^^ 3)) cm³");
}
```

## Example: knob on a shaft

```d
// A fluted knob for a potentiometer with a 6 mm D shaft, printable
// standing up as it is (no overhangs, no supports).
//
// Try it:
//  - drag the sliders in Parameters, or pick a preset;
//  - edit the code: the view updates as you type;
//  - right-click a face or an edge to add a fillet, a hole, a pocket...
//    the GUI writes the code for you.
module knob;

import std.shapes;
import hardware : M3, hole;

// @param puts a slider in the Parameters panel; @preset groups values under a name
@param("Diameter", min: 16.mm, max: 50.mm)
@preset("small", 18.mm) @preset("large", 36.mm)
immutable diameter = 26.mm;

@param("Height", min: 12.mm, max: 30.mm)
@preset("small", 16.mm) @preset("large", 20.mm)
immutable height = 17.mm;

@param("Flutes", min: 0, max: 30)
@preset("small", 10) @preset("large", 18)
immutable flutes = 14;

@param("Shaft clearance", min: 0.mm, max: 0.5.mm)
immutable clearance = 0.15.mm;

// the potentiometer shaft: 6 mm, with a flat leaving 4.5 mm
immutable shaftD = 6.mm;
immutable shaftFlat = 4.5.mm;
immutable shaftDepth = 10.mm;    // how far the shaft enters the knob

// the shape: a skirt at the bottom, a body narrowing towards the top
immutable r = diameter / 2;
immutable skirtR = r + 2.5.mm;
immutable skirtH = 1.6.mm;
immutable topR = r * 0.86;
immutable taper = atan((r - topR) / (height - skirtH));

/// A D-shaped prism: a cylinder with one side cut flat (towards +X).
Solid dShape(Length d, Length flat, Length h) =>
    cylinder(d: d, h: h) & box(d, d, h).move(x: flat - d);

/// The body as a profile (radius, height) turned around the axis.
Solid body()
{
    auto profile = polygon([
        vec(0.mm, 0.mm),
        vec(skirtR, 0.mm),
        vec(skirtR, skirtH),
        vec(r, skirtH + 2.5.mm),     // 45° up to the body: printable
        vec(topR, height),
        vec(0.mm, height),
    ]);
    return profile
        .revolve();
}

// @part marks a body to show and export; without a colour it is mint
@part
Solid knob()
{
    auto k = body()
        .fillet(edges.of(faces.top), r: 1.5.mm)
        .chamfer(edges.of(faces.bottom), d: 0.4.mm);

    // a shallow dish on top
    immutable dish = 4 * r;
    k -= sphere(r: dish).move(z: height + dish - 0.8.mm);

    // flutes: grooves leaning with the taper, half a step away from +X
    // so the pointer and the set screw fall between two of them
    immutable flute = 2 * PI * r / flutes * 0.55;
    foreach (i; 0 .. flutes)
        k -= cylinder(d: flute, h: height, center: true)
            .rotate(y: -taper)
            .move(x: (r + topR) / 2 + flute * 0.2, z: height / 2 + 5.mm)
            .rotate(z: (i + 0.5) * 360.deg / flutes);

    // the pointer: a groove across the top, in line with the flat of the shaft
    immutable pointer = topR * 0.6;
    k -= box(pointer, 1.2.mm, 3.mm)
        .move(x: topR - 2.5.mm - pointer / 2, z: height - 1.6.mm);

    // the shaft hole, ending in a cone so it prints without a bridge
    immutable hd = shaftD + 2 * clearance;
    k -= dShape(hd, shaftFlat + clearance, shaftDepth);
    k -= cone(d1: hd, d2: 0.mm, h: hd / 2).move(z: shaftDepth);

    // an M3 set screw pressing on the flat (hole() comes from the hardware library)
    k -= hole(M3, skirtR, "tap")
        .rotate(y: 90.deg)
        .move(x: skirtR, z: 6.mm);

    return k;
}

// a reference part: drawn see-through to check the fit, but left out of
// STL/3MF/STEP exports
@part("slategray", alpha: 0.4, export: false)
Solid shaft() => dShape(shaftD, shaftFlat, shaftDepth + 12.mm).move(z: -12.mm);

// unittests run after every evaluation: their output goes to the console
unittest
{
    assert(height >= shaftDepth + 5.mm, "the shaft would come out of the top: make the knob taller");
    writeln("knob: $(format("%.1f", knob.volume / 1.cm ^^ 3)) cm³");
}
```

## Library source: hardware

```d
module hardware;

import threads : threadedRod;

/// Metric screw sizes (ISO 4762 socket head cap screws, ISO 4032 nuts,
/// ISO 7089 washers) with the holes to print or drill for them.
struct Screw
{
    string name;
    Length d;           /// nominal diameter
    Length pitch;       /// coarse thread pitch
    Length tap;         /// pilot hole for tapping or self-tapping
    Length clearance;   /// clearance hole
    Length head;        /// head diameter
    Length headHeight;
    Length key;         /// hex key size (across flats)
    Length nut;         /// nut width across flats
    Length nutHeight;
    Length washer;      /// washer outer diameter
    Length insert;      /// hole for a heat-set threaded insert
    Length insertDepth;
}

immutable M2 = Screw("M2", 2.mm, 0.4.mm, 1.6.mm, 2.4.mm, 3.8.mm, 2.mm, 1.5.mm, 4.mm, 1.6.mm, 5.mm, 3.2.mm, 4.mm);
immutable M2_5 = Screw("M2.5", 2.5.mm, 0.45.mm, 2.05.mm, 2.9.mm, 4.5.mm, 2.5.mm, 2.mm, 5.mm, 2.mm, 6.mm, 3.6.mm, 5.mm);
immutable M3 = Screw("M3", 3.mm, 0.5.mm, 2.5.mm, 3.4.mm, 5.5.mm, 3.mm, 2.5.mm, 5.5.mm, 2.4.mm, 7.mm, 4.2.mm, 5.7.mm);
immutable M4 = Screw("M4", 4.mm, 0.7.mm, 3.3.mm, 4.5.mm, 7.mm, 4.mm, 3.mm, 7.mm, 3.2.mm, 9.mm, 5.6.mm, 8.1.mm);
immutable M5 = Screw("M5", 5.mm, 0.8.mm, 4.2.mm, 5.5.mm, 8.5.mm, 5.mm, 4.mm, 8.mm, 4.7.mm, 10.mm, 6.4.mm, 9.5.mm);
immutable M6 = Screw("M6", 6.mm, 1.mm, 5.mm, 6.6.mm, 10.mm, 6.mm, 5.mm, 10.mm, 5.2.mm, 12.mm, 8.mm, 12.7.mm);
immutable M8 = Screw("M8", 8.mm, 1.25.mm, 6.8.mm, 9.mm, 13.mm, 8.mm, 6.mm, 13.mm, 6.8.mm, 16.mm, 9.7.mm, 12.7.mm);

/// Hexagonal prism standing on XY, flats parallel to the X axis.
Solid hexPrism(Length acrossFlats, Length h)
{
    auto slab = box(acrossFlats * 2, acrossFlats, h);
    return slab & slab.rotate(z: 60) & slab.rotate(z: 120);
}

/// Socket head cap screw. The underside of the head lies on z = 0: the head
/// grows upwards and the shank downwards, so the screw drops into a hole.
/// threaded: true models the ISO thread (slower); otherwise the shank is plain.
Solid screw(Screw s, Length length, bool socket = true, bool threaded = false)
{
    auto shank = threaded
        ? threadedRod(s.d, s.pitch, length).move(z: -length)
        : cylinder(d: s.d, h: length)
            .chamfer(edges.filter(e => e.isCircle && e.mid.z < 1.mm), d: s.d * 0.1)
            .move(z: -length);
    auto head = cylinder(d: s.head, h: s.headHeight)
        .fillet(edges.filter(e => e.isCircle && e.mid.z > s.headHeight / 2), r: s.d * 0.12);
    if (socket)
        head -= hexPrism(s.key, s.headHeight).move(z: s.headHeight * 0.45);
    return head + shank;
}

/// Hex nut standing on z = 0, with the corners chamfered on both faces.
/// threaded: true cuts the ISO thread in the hole.
Solid nut(Screw s, bool threaded = false)
{
    // a cone narrow at the face and wider than the corners at mid height
    auto lower = cone(d1: s.nut * 0.95, d2: s.nut * 1.4, h: s.nutHeight / 2);
    auto upper = lower.mirror(Z).move(z: s.nutHeight);
    auto body = hexPrism(s.nut, s.nutHeight) & (lower + upper);
    if (threaded)
        return body - threadedRod(s.d, s.pitch, s.nutHeight + 2 * s.pitch, chamfer: false).move(z: -s.pitch);
    return body - cylinder(d: s.d, h: 3 * s.nutHeight, center: true);
}

/// Flat washer standing on z = 0.
Solid washer(Screw s) => cylinder(d: s.washer, h: s.d * 0.2) - cylinder(d: s.clearance, h: s.d, center: true);

/// A hole to subtract, with its top on z = 0 going down `depth`:
/// "clearance" (the screw passes), "tap" (pilot hole for the thread),
/// "insert" (heat-set insert), "counterbore" (clearance with room for the
/// head) or "countersink" (for flat heads).
Solid hole(Screw s, Length depth, string kind = "clearance")
{
    switch (kind)
    {
    case "clearance":
        return cylinder(d: s.clearance, h: depth + 0.01.mm).move(z: -depth);
    case "tap":
        return cylinder(d: s.tap, h: depth + 0.01.mm).move(z: -depth);
    case "insert":
        return cylinder(d: s.insert, h: s.insertDepth).move(z: -s.insertDepth)
            + cylinder(d: s.tap, h: depth).move(z: -depth);
    case "counterbore":
        return cylinder(d: s.head + 0.6.mm, h: s.headHeight + 0.2.mm).move(z: -s.headHeight - 0.2.mm)
            + cylinder(d: s.clearance, h: depth).move(z: -depth);
    case "countersink":
        return cone(d1: s.clearance, d2: s.d * 2, h: s.d / 2).move(z: -s.d / 2)
            + cylinder(d: s.clearance, h: depth).move(z: -depth);
    default:
        assert(false, "hole kind must be clearance, tap, insert, counterbore or countersink, not " ~ kind);
    }
}

/// A pocket to trap a nut, from z = 0 going down `depth` (with a little clearance).
Solid nutTrap(Screw s, Length depth, Length clearance = 0.2.mm) =>
    hexPrism(s.nut + 2 * clearance, depth + 0.01.mm).move(z: -depth);
```

## Library source: threads

```d
module threads;

/// ISO metric threads (basic profile, 60°). Threads are real geometry: they
/// print and export to STEP, but take longer to compute than plain shapes.

/// Height of the thread tooth for a pitch (from the minor to the major diameter).
Length toothHeight(Length pitch) => 0.5413 * pitch;

/// A threaded rod of nominal diameter `d` standing on z = 0, with the ends
/// chamfered (chamfer: false leaves them square).
Solid threadedRod(Length d, Length pitch, Length length, bool chamfer = true, bool left = false)
{
    immutable h = toothHeight(pitch);
    immutable minor = d - 2 * h;
    immutable overlap = 0.1 * pitch;   // the tooth sinks into the core so that they fuse
    // swept along the helix: the profile's +x points to the axis, +y along it
    auto tooth = polygon([vec(overlap, -0.375 * pitch), vec(-h, -pitch / 16), vec(-h, pitch / 16),
                          vec(overlap, 0.375 * pitch)]);
    auto ridge = tooth.sweep(helix(d: minor, pitch: pitch, height: length + 2 * pitch, left: left), frenet: true)
        .move(z: -pitch);
    // the core is longer than the ridge: the ends are trimmed afterwards
    auto core = cylinder(d: minor + 0.02.mm, h: length + 4 * pitch).move(z: -2 * pitch);
    auto envelope = cylinder(d: d + 0.02.mm, h: length);
    if (chamfer)
        envelope = envelope.chamfer(edges.circles, d: h);
    return (core + ridge) & envelope;
}

/// A tool to subtract for an internal thread that a `d` screw fits, from
/// z = 0 going down `depth`. `clearance` widens it for printed parts.
Solid tappedHole(Length d, Length pitch, Length depth, Length clearance = 0.15.mm) =>
    threadedRod(d + 2 * clearance, pitch, depth + pitch, chamfer: false).move(z: -depth);
```

## Library source: gears

```d
module gears;

/// Involute spur gears and racks. `m` is the module (pitch diameter / teeth):
/// two gears mesh when they have the same module and pressure angle, with
/// their centres `centerDistance(m, z1, z2)` apart.

Length pitchDiameter(Length m, int teeth) => m * teeth;
Length outsideDiameter(Length m, int teeth) => m * (teeth + 2);
Length rootDiameter(Length m, int teeth) => m * (teeth - 2.5);
Length centerDistance(Length m, int teeth1, int teeth2) => m * (teeth1 + teeth2) / 2;

/// Angle of the involute of a circle of radius rb at radius r.
double involute(Length rb, Length r)
{
    immutable t = sqrt((r / rb) ^^ 2 - 1);
    return t - atan(t) / 1.rad;
}

/// The outline of a spur gear centred on the origin, a tooth on +X.
/// backlash thins the teeth (measured on the pitch circle) so that printed
/// gears do not bind.
Profile gearProfile(Length m, int teeth, Angle pressure = 20.deg, Length backlash = 0.1.mm, int steps = 6)
{
    assert(teeth >= 6, "a gear needs at least 6 teeth");
    immutable r = m * teeth / 2;
    immutable rb = r * cos(pressure);
    immutable ra = r + m;
    immutable rf = r - 1.25 * m;
    // half the tooth thickness on the pitch circle, as an angle, plus the involute offset
    immutable half = PI / (2 * teeth) - backlash / (2 * r) + involute(rb, r);
    immutable start = max(rb, rf);
    Vec2[] pts;
    foreach (k; 0 .. teeth)
    {
        immutable c = 2 * PI * k / teeth;
        Vec2[] flank;    // from the root to the tip, on the side of negative angles
        if (rf < rb)
            flank ~= vec(rf * cos(c - half), rf * sin(c - half));
        foreach (i; 0 .. steps + 1)
        {
            immutable rr = start + (ra - start) * i / steps;
            immutable a = c - half + involute(rb, rr);
            flank ~= vec(rr * cos(a), rr * sin(a));
        }
        pts ~= flank;
        // the other flank, mirrored around the tooth's centre line, from the tip to the root
        foreach_reverse (p; flank)
        {
            immutable a = 2 * c - atan2(p.y, p.x) / 1.rad;
            immutable rr = sqrt(p.x ^^ 2 + p.y ^^ 2);
            pts ~= vec(rr * cos(a), rr * sin(a));
        }
    }
    return polygon(pts);
}

/// A spur gear standing on z = 0, with an optional bore.
Solid spurGear(Length m, int teeth, Length thickness, Length bore = 0.mm, Angle pressure = 20.deg,
    Length backlash = 0.1.mm)
{
    auto g = gearProfile(m, teeth, pressure, backlash).extrude(thickness);
    if (bore > 0.mm)
        g -= cylinder(d: bore, h: 3 * thickness, center: true);
    return g;
}

/// A straight rack along +X starting at x = 0, teeth up, pitch line at y = 0.
Solid rack(Length m, int teeth, Length thickness, Length base = 0.mm, Angle pressure = 20.deg)
{
    immutable p = PI * m;
    immutable b = base > 0.mm ? base : 2 * m;
    immutable t = tan(pressure);
    Vec2[] pts = [vec(0.mm, -1.25 * m - b)];
    foreach (k; 0 .. teeth)
    {
        immutable x0 = k * p;
        pts ~= [vec(x0, -1.25 * m), vec(x0 + p / 4 - 1.25 * m * t, -1.25 * m), vec(x0 + p / 4 + m * t, m),
                vec(x0 + 3 * p / 4 - m * t, m), vec(x0 + 3 * p / 4 + 1.25 * m * t, -1.25 * m)];
    }
    pts ~= [vec(teeth * p, -1.25 * m), vec(teeth * p, -1.25 * m - b)];
    return polygon(pts).extrude(thickness);
}
```

## Library source: hinges

```d
module hinges;

/// The two leaves of a hinge, printed in place: they come out of the
/// printer already joined and turn around the X axis.
struct Hinge
{
    Solid fixed;    /// the leaf on -Y, with the pin
    Solid moving;   /// the leaf on +Y, turning around the pin
}

/// A print-in-place hinge along X, centred on the origin, leaves lying flat
/// on z = 0 and the axis at z = thickness. `knuckles` alternate between
/// the leaves (odd numbers keep it symmetric).
Hinge hinge(Length length = 40.mm, Length width = 15.mm, Length thickness = 3.mm, int knuckles = 5,
    Length clearance = 0.4.mm)
{
    assert(knuckles >= 3, "a hinge needs at least 3 knuckles");
    immutable outer = 2 * thickness;           // knuckle diameter
    immutable pin = outer * 0.45;
    immutable segment = length / knuckles;

    /// Knuckle i with the web that joins it to its leaf (side -1 or +1).
    Solid knuckle(int i, int side)
    {
        immutable x0 = -length / 2 + i * segment + (i > 0 ? clearance / 2 : 0.mm);
        immutable x1 = -length / 2 + (i + 1) * segment - (i < knuckles - 1 ? clearance / 2 : 0.mm);
        immutable reach = outer / 2 + clearance;
        auto web = box(x1 - x0, reach, thickness).move(x: (x0 + x1) / 2, y: side * reach / 2);
        return cylinder(d: outer, h: x1 - x0).rotate(y: 90).move(x: x0, z: thickness) + web;
    }

    Solid a = box(length, width, thickness).move(y: -width / 2 - outer / 2 - clearance);
    Solid b = box(length, width, thickness).move(y: width / 2 + outer / 2 + clearance);
    foreach (i; 0 .. knuckles)
    {
        if (i % 2 == 0)
            a += knuckle(i, -1);
        else
            b += knuckle(i, 1);
    }
    // the pin belongs to the fixed leaf and runs through the moving knuckles with clearance
    a += cylinder(d: pin, h: length - 2 * clearance).rotate(y: 90).move(x: -length / 2 + clearance, z: thickness);
    foreach (i; 0 .. knuckles)
        if (i % 2 == 1)
            b -= cylinder(d: pin + 2 * clearance, h: length).rotate(y: 90).move(x: -length / 2, z: thickness);
    return Hinge(a, b);
}
```

## Library source: snaps

```d
module snaps;

/// Cantilever snap-fit hooks. The hook stands on z = 0 and leans out along
/// +X; print it standing so the layers run along the beam.

/// A hook: a flexible beam `length` long with a barb `overhang` deep at the
/// top. `lead` is the slope that pushes it aside when inserting.
Solid snapHook(Length length = 10.mm, Length thickness = 1.5.mm, Length width = 5.mm, Length overhang = 1.mm,
    Angle lead = 30.deg)
{
    immutable barb = overhang / tan(lead);     // height of the sloped face
    auto profile = polygon([vec(0.mm, 0.mm), vec(thickness, 0.mm), vec(thickness, length),
                            vec(thickness + overhang, length), vec(thickness, length + barb),
                            vec(0.mm, length + barb)]);
    // drawn in the XY plane (y up the beam), then stood up
    return profile.extrude(width).move(z: -width / 2).rotate(x: 90).move(y: 0.mm);
}

/// The slot a hook clicks into, to subtract from the mating wall: a window
/// `clearance` larger than the barb.
Solid snapSlot(Length thickness = 1.5.mm, Length width = 5.mm, Length overhang = 1.mm, Length wall = 2.mm,
    Length clearance = 0.3.mm) =>
    box(thickness + overhang + 2 * clearance, width + 2 * clearance, wall + 1.mm)
        .move(x: (thickness + overhang) / 2, z: -0.5.mm);
```

## Library source: enclosures

```d
module enclosures;

import hardware : Screw, M3, hole;

/// Boxes with rounded corners and enclosures with lids.

/// A box centred in X and Y on z = 0, with vertical edges rounded by `r`.
Solid roundedBox(Length x, Length y, Length z, Length r = 3.mm) =>
    box(x, y, z).fillet(edges.parallel(Z), r: r);

/// An open box: walls `wall` thick, open on top.
Solid tray(Length x, Length y, Length z, Length wall = 2.mm, Length r = 3.mm) =>
    roundedBox(x, y, z, r).shell(open: faces.top, thickness: wall);

/// A base and a lid that fit together, both standing on z = 0.
struct Enclosure
{
    Solid base;
    Solid lid;
}

/// An enclosure with `inner` free space (x, y, z), a lid with a lip that
/// fits inside the base, and a screw post in each corner.
Enclosure enclosure(Vec3 inner, Length wall = 2.mm, Length r = 3.mm, Length lidHeight = 4.mm,
    Screw screw = M3, Length clearance = 0.2.mm)
{
    immutable ox = inner.x + 2 * wall, oy = inner.y + 2 * wall;
    auto base = tray(ox, oy, inner.z + wall, wall, r);
    auto lid = roundedBox(ox, oy, wall, r);
    // the lip: a thin ring that slides into the base
    immutable lx = inner.x - 2 * clearance, ly = inner.y - 2 * clearance;
    auto lip = roundedBox(lx, ly, lidHeight, max(r - wall, 0.5.mm)) - roundedBox(lx - 2 * wall, ly - 2 * wall, lidHeight * 3,
        max(r - 2 * wall, 0.5.mm)).move(z: -lidHeight);
    lid += lip.move(z: wall);

    // posts: tapped for the screw in the base, clearance holes in the lid
    immutable px = inner.x / 2 - screw.d * 1.2, py = inner.y / 2 - screw.d * 1.2;
    foreach (sx; [-1, 1])
        foreach (sy; [-1, 1])
        {
            auto post = cylinder(d: screw.d * 2.4, h: inner.z + wall - lidHeight - clearance);
            base += post.move(x: sx * px, y: sy * py);
            base -= hole(screw, inner.z, "tap").move(x: sx * px, y: sy * py, z: inner.z + wall - lidHeight - clearance);
            lid -= cylinder(d: screw.clearance, h: 10 * wall, center: true).move(x: sx * px, y: sy * py);
            lid -= cylinder(d: screw.d * 2.4 + 2 * clearance, h: lidHeight * 2).move(x: sx * px, y: sy * py, z: wall);
        }
    return Enclosure(base, lid);
}
```
